newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's Kaduna oil refinery shut for repairs.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's Kaduna oil refinery shut for repairs.

text.p: Nigeria's northern oil refinery at Kaduna with installed capacity of 110,000 barrels per day (bpd) has been shut down for repairs, local newspapers reported on Wednesday.
The papers did not say how long the refinery would be closed for, or whether it was closed for turn around maintenance which had been scheduled for this year.

The majority state-owned Daily Times said that Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) had put in place contingency plans to obtain fuel for northern parts of the country from the southern Warri refinery.

Nigeria, despite producing over two million barrels of crude oil per day, suffers from frequent bouts of fuel scarcity. Its four refineries, which are poorly maintained, run far from their designed capacity of 445,000 bpd.
After weeks of paralysing petrol shortages earlier this year the military government ordered massive imports of fuel, but distribution problems mean that local scarcities persist.
